literal: The fruit of virtue is this, saying so is not needed; it is seen between the palanquin bearer and the rider.
translation: There is no need to explain the fruit of virtue with words; it is plainly visible in the contrast between the bearer of the palanquin and the one who rides in it.
modern: அறத்தின் பயன் இது என்று நூல்களைக் கொண்டு விளக்க வேண்டியதில்லை; பல்லக்கைத் தூக்கிச் செல்பவனுக்கும் அதில் ஏறிச் செல்பவனுக்கும் இடையே உள்ள வேறுபாட்டிலேயே அது விளங்கும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid, everyday image to illustrate the self-evident nature of the fruits of virtue. The word 'ஆறு' can mean 'path' or 'fruit/result'; in this context, 'fruit' or 'consequence' fits best. The poet argues that one does not need elaborate philosophical arguments to prove the power of virtue. Instead, the stark contrast between the physical toil of the palanquin bearer ('பொறுத்தான்') and the comfort of the rider ('ஊர்ந்தான்') serves as a direct, visible demonstration of how past actions shape present circumstances.
